title: Balance
prompt: a two-pan balance with a set of small masses on a table with three buttons: “Load” places an unknown mass in one pan; “Add weight” lowers the other pan toward equilibrium; “Compare” swaps the objects and checks the balance; see-through reveals the central knife-edge fulcrum, equal arms and opposing torques
blurb: A bench teaching adaptation of the book’s equal-arm balance compares an unknown object with known masses in suspended pans.

identity.note: Levers / Levers in action / First-class levers / Balance, page 22. Equal arms compare an object with known weights.

adaptationDecision.reason: Distinct from the unequal-arm beam-scale and the three-lever platform-scales. Existing Cavendish measures attraction through torsion of a wire, rather than equal-arm weighing.

prompt.note: Faithful. Loading, adding known masses and exchanging pans preserve equal-arm weighing. Use the suspended pans pictured on page 22. A knife edge is a plausible construction detail, not proved by this caption. Do not silently substitute the parallel-link Roberval apparatus on page 24.
prompt.apparatusRelation: Bench or scale teaching adaptation of a named book example. Controls, fixtures and test specimens stage the lesson and are not claimed as the book apparatus.

constructionSources.supports: Representative central and end knife edges, bearing plates, beam pointer and fixed index.
A real two-pan equal-arm balance oscillates about a center knife edge and is read with a fixed pointer scale. This simplified teaching model does not reproduce the NIST instrument.

teachingAdaptation.fixtures: A tabletop, a blue 150 g unknown artifact and three 50 g reference masses stage equal-arm weighing. They are not claimed as the original book apparatus.

actions.Load: An implicit operator carries the unknown from the table to one pan. Repeating returns contents to the table and reloads the same object.
actions.Add weight: An implicit operator transfers one 50 g reference mass from the table to the other pan. Three masses establish equilibrium.
actions.Compare: An implicit operator exchanges the contents around opposite sides of the support. Fixed pan assemblies stay in place. Equal or unequal balance is checked after the exchange.

simplifications: Tilt and settling are illustrative, exaggerated and time-compressed, not calibrated angular mass measurements.
The equal empty pan assemblies cancel. Beam center of mass lies below the fulcrum for stable equilibrium.
Moment readout uses supported specimen mass times 9.81 m/s2 times the horizontal projection of a 16 cm arm. It omits equal tare torques.
Arrows and 16 cm arm dimensions are teaching overlays and do not count as anatomy.
No mechanical or powered loader, precision arrest mechanism, Roberval linkage or automatic repair is implied.
